claims.claim: ⚠️ **Children and adolescents with eating disorders can appear well despite being medically unstable** — cardiovascular complications, electrolyte imbalance, dehydration.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **They may present with suicidal ideation, escalating compensatory behaviours or comorbid psychiatric disorders needing urgent mental health assessment.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No psychiatric disorder has a higher mortality than anorexia nervosa.** ARFID can also cause medical instability; seek specialist input, but admission criteria are similar.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Applies up to 18 years**; age limits for specialist services vary by location.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **History in all patients:** current, pre-morbid and highest weight and speed of loss · fainting, dizziness, palpitations, cold intolerance, constipation, abdominal symptoms · menstrual history · **mood, suicide and self-harm risk** · HEEADSSS.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine:** weight, height, BMI, temperature, and **postural HR and BP lying to standing, 2–3 minutes apart**; look for undernutrition, purging signs (enamel erosion, Russell's sign, enlarged salivary glands) and acrocyanosis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bloods:** FBE, UEC, Ca, Mg, PO4, LFTs, glucose, ketones, VBG; **if new diagnosis** add ESR, thyroid function, coeliac screen. **12-lead ECG**; urinalysis; βhCG if amenorrhoeic.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Strongly consider admission for medical instability: any red-flag feature or multiple amber-flag features.** Talk to the on-call paediatric or adolescent medicine clinician about unit placement, or if unsure.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Heart rate awake — consider admission:** under 50 bpm or postural rise over 50 bpm · **concern:** 50–60 bpm or postural rise over 20 bpm · **moderate risk:** over 60 bpm with normal postural change.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Blood pressure — consider admission:** SBP under 80 or postural drop over 20 mmHg · **concern:** SBP under 90 or postural drop over 15 mmHg · **moderate risk:** normal resting SBP and postural drop under 15 mmHg.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Temperature — consider admission:** under 35.5°C · **concern:** under 36.0°C · **moderate risk:** over 36.0°C. **Syncope** — consider admission: recurrent; concern: occasional; moderate risk: none, or pre-syncope only.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hydration — consider admission:** fluid refusal over 48 hours or severe dehydration (over 10%) · **concern:** moderate dehydration (5–9%) or severe fluid restriction · **moderate risk:** minimal restriction, no more than mild dehydration (under 5%).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Weight loss — consider admission:** over 1 kg/week or over 15% in 3–6 months · **concern:** 0.5 to 1 kg/week · **moderate risk:** under 0.5 kg/week or fluctuating. **Percent of median BMI:** under 70% · 70–80% · over 80%.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Also listed as signs of medical instability** (column not recoverable): **QTc over 450 msec or other significant ECG abnormality**; hypophosphataemia under 0.9 mmol/L, hypokalaemia under 3.0 mmol/L, hypoglycaemia under 3.0 mmol/L, hyponatraemia under 130 mmol/L; transaminases over 3 times normal; Hb under 100 g/L.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Refeeding syndrome:** potentially fatal fluid and electrolyte shifts on re-feeding an undernourished child; **its hallmark is hypophosphataemia.** Large oral or IV fluid volumes risk fluid overload and cardiac compromise.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Start nutrition and hydration only after investigations are reviewed and a plan is agreed with the admitting team** — then as soon as possible, ideally in the ED.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If feeding starts in the ED, consider first: thiamine 100 mg orally and phosphate 500 mg (elemental) orally.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider ongoing cardiac monitoring** (discuss first with the admitting consultant) when there is severe electrolyte disturbance such as K under 2.5 mmol/L, **HR under 45 bpm, or HR under 40 bpm asleep.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Medically stable, no urgent mental health need:** new diagnosis — discuss outpatient management with the on-call consultant; known diagnosis — refer to the local service or the patient's known ED clinician.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If there are mental health concerns, discuss with the local mental health team** — urgent assessment may be needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric or adolescent team** if medically unstable or needing admission, at first presentation, or to plan follow-up. **Transfer** if care exceeds the local facility.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge only when medically stable, mental health assessment is complete, and follow-up is arranged.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of Eating Disorders in the Emergency Department' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_Eating_Disorders_in_the_Emergency_Department/, retrieved 2026-09-23
